JUDGMENT
Three complaints are filed by the complainant against accused under Section 200 of Cr.P.C for the offence punishable U/s 138 & 142 of Negotiable Instruments Act.

They are in respect of one single transaction and contentions advanced and defences taken are similar in all three cases, but there are three different cheques for three different amounts and presented on different dates.
Hence, it is stated that they are filed separately before this court.
In the complaint it is stated that, complainant company is in the business of property development since 35 years.

That accused no.2 and 3 approached the complainant company stating that they are the partners of partnership firm in the name and style of M/s. Good Home Ventures registered under Indian Partnership Act and they are responsible for the day to day affairs of the accused no.1 firm.

That during 2005 the State Government issued notification for granting of Transferable Development Rights (TDR) for the lands surrendered to the BBMP for public purposes like road widening/parks/playgrounds and other civic amenities by using Development Right Certificate (DRC).

That one Sri.Goutham Reddy who was client of accused company, approached the BBMP to surrender a portion of land subject to acquisition voluntarily in favour of the BBMP with respect to Sy.No.116/2 & 116/3 Bidarahalli village, Bidarahalli hobli, Bengaluru East Taluk.
3. Further it is stated that Mr. Goutham Reddy offered to sell the TDR to the accused company.
The accused company entered into Agreement of Sale dated 03.11.2014 for purchase of the said TDR.

Further on 30.01.2015 two deed of sale of transferable development rights was entered between Sri.Goutham Reedy, accused and the complainant with respect to TDR and the accused have nominated the complaint for the purchase of TDR.
Accordingly, complainant company paid sale consideration amount of Rs.2,20,07,900/ to Sri.Goutham Reddy and the accused for the said TDR.

That accused herein to reimburse the SCCH12 4 C.C.No.12015/2021 TDR amount have executed the registered agreement of sale on 21.10.2020 in favour of the complainant company by offering the immovable property being the residential villa bearing No.B1 having village Khata No.167/B1 measuring 2990 sq.ft of sital area and 3005 sqft of built up area in the development known as NVT Orchid Garden for sale consideration of INR3,59,27,991/.

 REASONS  SCCH12 8 C.C.No.12015/2021 11.
Point No
. i : The above complaint is filed against the accused for the offence punishable under Section 138 of N.I. Act.
To prove its case, Managing Director of the complainant got examined as P.W.1.
He reiterated the complaint averments in his chief examination.
He has produced original cheque at Ex.P.1.

It shows, accused no.2 and 3 have drawn cheque No.000370 dt.31.08.2021 for Rs.1,50,00,000/ drawn on HDFC Bank, Church Street branch, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru towards discharge of liability in favour of complainant bank after placing their signature on it.

The said cheque was presented for encasement at HDFC Bank,
Richmond road, Bengaluru and it is returned with shara 'Account blocked' on 08.09.2021 vide bank endorsement produced at Ex.P.2.
The Legal notice is produced at Ex.P.3, it is issued on 07.10.2021 which is in time.
The postal receipts are produced at Ex.P.4 and postal acknowledgement is produced at Ex.P.5.
It shows that the notice is served on accused.
In statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C accused have admitted the receipt of notice.
12. In statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C accused stated that, cheque is forcefully taken by the complainant which indicates that issuance of cheque to complainant.
The signature on cheque is not disputed.
The cheque belongs to the account of the accused.
Therefore, there is presumption under Section 139 of N.I. Act that holder of the cheque has received the same in discharge of legally enforceable debt or liability in his favour.
All the ingredients which are necessary to constitute the offence under Section 138 of N.I.Act are fulfilled bythe complainant.
As SCCH12 9 C.C.No.12015/2021 such, presumption under Section 139 of N.I. Act deserves to be drawn in favour of complainant.
Accordingly, such presumption is drawn.
13. Now, whether accused has rebutted the said presumption will have to be examined.
It is the defense of the accused that cheque is forcefully taken by the complainant and his house is also mortgaged in favour of complainant.

If cheque is taken forcefully from the hands of accused,
accused had all the opportunity to approach competent legal or police authority to take action against the complainant for forcefully compelling the accused to do certain act against his will and interest.
He could also issue stop payment instruction to the bank not to encahs the cheque as it is forecefully taken by him against his interest.
But no such action is taken by the accused against the complainant and cheque is returned for the reason acccount blocked.
Therefore, the defence that cheque is forcefully taken cannot be accepted.

14. Another defence of the accused is that, complainant could have used the TDRs till 2019 and they had time till then, but they have not utilized it and when they thought of utilizing it, government has changed the rules and regulations and they could not utilize the same.
Then they called accused and stated that since TDRs could not be utilized and asked to return the money paid.

By this defence accused contended that, even though complainant had opportunity to utilize TDRs within 5 years,
instead of utilizing it they kept mum for several years and then approached accused for repayment Embassy Classic Pvt. Ltd vs Good Home Ventures on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57121999/
5 of money only on the SCCH12 10 C.C.No.12015/2021 ground that TDRs could not be utilized.

Now,
it is necessary to notice that in the cross examination of P.W.1, complainant deposed that the TDRs turned out to be fake, and accused agreed to return the amount.
This statement of P.W.1 is not denied by accused.
15. Accused had all the opportunity to contend that TDRs were never fake, but complainant himself intentionally not used it, but no such contention is taken by the accused.
He admitted to reimburse the amount instead.
In the complaint it is stated that, accused agreed to reimburse the money paid to the TDRs.
The said statement is also not denied by the accused, therefore the defence of the accused that, complainant should have used TDRs within 2019 cannot be accepted.
16. Yet another defence of the accused is that he never received the money as loan nor there is any debt for which property could be mortgaged.
He contended that some conditions in the mortgage deed and sale agreement are all one sided and gives an indication it is done under the threat, force and undue influence.
It is necessary to notice that such contention is never taken at the initial stage by issuing reply to legal notice.
Though accused contended that he issued reply to notice, the same is not produced before the court.
If such defence was taken, at initial stage, accused had an opportunity to produce the reply before the court and questioned about the same to PW1.
But no such question is posed to PW1.
In fact on entire reading of cross examination of PW1, there is no suggestion about the defence of SCCH12 11 C.C.No.12015/2021 the accused.
Nothing helpful to the defence of the accused is elicited from the mouth of PW1.
Therefore the contention that documents are executed by threat, coercion or undue influence cannot be accepted.
That apart, those documents are of the year 2020 and this case is being decided in 2024.
Till now accused has not taken any action against the complainant in respect of sale agreement or mortgage deed before any court of law.
Hence, even that defence is not acceptable.
17. Now coming to the fact of issuance of cheque regarding liability, court has to examine whether accused is liable to pay totally, Rs.3,59,27,991/ as alleged by the complainant.

It is argued before this court that there was no liability at all in respect of the transaction of the year 2014 which in fact happened between the original owner of the land, complainant and the accused which is tripartite agreement.
However no defence of time barred debt or liability is taken by the accused either by issuing reply to legal notice, or in cross examination of PW1, or in defence evidence.

No such question is posed to P.W.1.
18.

On perusal of Ex.P.9 it can be seen that it is registered sale deed of Transferable Development Rights (TDR) executed on 30.01.2015 between one Goutham Reddy, the accused Good Home Ventures herein, and complainant Embassy Classics Pvt.Ltd.

As per the said sale deed Goutham Reddy being owner of the land mentioned in the sale deed has sold the DRC I..e, Development Right Certificate issued in respect of BBMP notified land as per Notification dated 29.07.2009 in favour of SCCH12 12 C.C.No.12015/2021 complainant herein.

It is mentioned in the sale deed that, Goutham Reddy voluntarily surrendered the land to BBMP and in consideration of such surrender BBMP has granted DRC in respect of 459/Sq mtrs to be utilized as per revised master plan.

It is also mentioned that Good Home Ventures i.e., accused herein has entered into sale agreement with Goutham Reddy and as per the agreement Good Home Ventures can purchase the TDR in its name or it can Embassy Classic Pvt. sentences.text: That Good Home Ventures has nominated Embassy Classic ie.,complainant herein for purchase of TDRs from Goutham Reddy.
19. As per the said sale deed, Goutham Reddy is owner, Good Home Ventures is confirming party and Embassy Classic is the transferee or purchaser of the DRC.
The amount of Rs.16,35,000/ is paid to Goutham Reddy and Rs.21,19,900/ is paid to Good Home Ventures (Accused) who is confirming party under that document.
The said amount is paid to the accused as reimbursement of sale consideration paid by him to the owner and also towards nomination fee for having nominated the transferee i.e., complainant.

Similarly as per another sale deed produced at Ex.P.10 one Chinamma and Goutham Reddy are owners of property and amount of Rs.63,08,800/ is paid by complainant to the owners and amount of Rs.1,18,24,758/ is paid by complainant to the accused towards reimbursement of sale consideration paid by him to the owners and also towards nomination fee for having nominated the transferee.

On careful perusal of the entire registered sale deeds there is no acceptance SCCH12 13 C.C.No.12015/2021 of liability by the accused to pay or return the amount paid by complainant if the TDRs cannot be utilized.

However, there is clause in both the sale deeds at condition no.3(g) that in the event BBMP cancels TDRs or if there is any defect or prior claim against the transferors or transferee looses his right over the TDR, the transferor shall compensate the transferee for losses causes to the transferee.
Therefore, as per the sale deed it is transferor who is liable to compensate the complainant in case of any defects and it is not the confirming party.
20. Now the question is when transferor is liable to refund the amount, how confirming party holds liability to pay the amount to complainant.
The answer is admission by the accused.
There are two admitted documents executed by the accused in favour of the complaint. I.e.
Ex . P.11
registered agreement of sale and Ex.P.12 original mortgage deed in which accused has admitted that he is liable to reimburse the consideration and cost incurred for purchase of the TDRs
. In fact, there was no liability on his part as per Ex.P.9 and 10 to reimburse the consideration.

But in Ex.P.11 and 12 sale agreement and mortgage deed there is mention about one undertaking given by accused to complainant admitted his liability to return the consideration and cost in curred in purchase of TDRs.
These documents are not questioned and challenged by accused.
Complainant cannot rely upon the terms of mortgage deed as it is not registered and only stamp duty is paid.
Mere payment of stamo duty will not cure the defect of registration.

Therefore, accused having admitted his liability and admitted the issuance of cheque and not disputed his signature and failed to rebut the presumption, he is liable to pay the cheque amount to the complainant.
He admitted the receipt of part consideration under TDR sale deeds.
It is not his case that, TDRS were not fake or that he had never received any consideration under the TDR sale deeds.
He has also not taken any action against the complainant for alleged forceful or pressurized execution of documents.
Instead he stated that, he sought time to pay the amount and also given the cheque as security.
Hence, I am of the opinion that accused has to be convicted in the above case and he shall be directed to pay the amount mentioned in the cheque to the complainant.

22 However, in the opinion of this court, double the cheque amount cannot be ordered as compensation in this case, in view of the fact that the compensation involved is above one crore which is huge amount and also for the reason that under the original TDR sale deed of the year 2015, there was no condition that confirming party should make good of loss borne by the transferee.

Only when the accused admitted his liability, SCCH12 16 C.C.No.12015/2021 executed documents, and issued cheques in favour of the complainant and they are dishonoured, his liability to pay the amount has been arisen.

Hence, on that ground, this court deems it fit that if the accused is convicted for Rs.1,50,10,000/ and the amount of Rs.1,50,00,000/ is awarded as compensation to the complainant and remaining amount of Rs.10,000/ is awarded as state expenses the interest of justice would be met.
Since amount involved is huge, one month time shall be granted to accused to pay the compensation to the complainant.

Hence, I hold this point in the 'Affirmative'.

9. The points that arise for my consideration are as follows:
i.
Whether complainant proves beyond reasonable doubt that accused has issued cheque No.000370 dt.31.08.2021 drawn on HDFC Bank, Church Street, Bangalore for Rs.1,50,00,000/ in discharge of liability and the same is dishonored for ''Account Blocked' and even after issuance of legal notice dt.07.10.2021 accused has not repaid the cheque amount and thereby accused committed offense punishable under Section 138 R/w Sec 142 of Negotiable Instruments Act ?
ii. What order ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The cheque belongs to the account of the accused.
All the ingredients which are necessary to constitute the offence under Section 138 of N.I.Act are fulfilled bythe complainant.
As SCCH12 9 C.C.No.12015/2021 such, presumption under Section 139 of N.I. Act deserves to be drawn in favour of complainant.
Accordingly, such presumption is drawn.
If cheque is taken forcefully from the hands of accused,
accused had all the opportunity to approach competent legal or police authority to take action against the complainant for forcefully compelling the accused to do certain act against his will and interest.
He could also issue stop payment instruction to the bank not to encahs the cheque as it is forecefully taken by him against his interest.
But no such action is taken by the accused against the complainant and cheque is returned for the reason acccount blocked.
Therefore, the defence that cheque is forcefully taken cannot be accepted.
Therefore the contention that documents are executed by threat, coercion or undue influence cannot be accepted.
On careful perusal of the entire registered sale deeds there is no acceptance SCCH12 13 C.C.No.12015/2021 of liability by the accused to pay or return the amount paid by complainant if the TDRs cannot be utilized.
However, there is clause in both the sale deeds at condition no.3(g) that in the event BBMP cancels TDRs or if there is any defect or prior claim against the transferors or transferee looses his right over the TDR, the transferor shall compensate the transferee for losses causes to the transferee.
Therefore, as per the sale deed it is transferor who is liable to compensate the complainant in case of any defects and it is not the confirming party.
Mere payment of stamo duty will not cure the defect of registration.
Therefore, accused having admitted his liability and admitted the issuance of cheque and not disputed his signature and failed to rebut the presumption, he is liable to pay the cheque amount to the complainant.
He admitted the receipt of part consideration under TDR sale deeds.
It is not his case that, TDRS were not fake or that he had never received any consideration under the TDR sale deeds.
Instead he stated that, he sought time to pay the amount and also given the cheque as security.
22 However, in the opinion of this court, double the cheque amount cannot be ordered as compensation in this case, in view of the fact that the compensation involved is above one crore which is huge amount and also for the reason that under the original TDR sale deed of the year 2015, there was no condition that confirming party should make good of loss borne by the transferee.
Only when the accused admitted his liability, SCCH12 16 C.C.No.12015/2021 executed documents, and issued cheques in favour of the complainant and they are dishonoured, his liability to pay the amount has been arisen.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Since amount involved is huge, one month time shall be granted to accused to pay the compensation to the complainant.
Hence, I hold this point in the 'Affirmative'.
23. Point No.ii
: In view of above reasons, I proceed to pass the following :
Embassy Classic Pvt. Ltd vs Good Home Ventures on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57121999/
8 ORDER Acting under Sec. 255(2) of Cr. P. C. accused no.2 and 3 are convicted for the offence punishable under Sec. 138 of Negotiable instruments Act.
Consequently, accused no. 2 and 3 are directed to pay a fine of Rs.1,50,10,000/
within period of one month from the date of this judgment, failing which they shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one year each.
Under Sec.357(1) of Cr.P.C. out of fine amount an amount of Rs.1,50,00,000/ shall be paid to complainant as compensation and remaining Rs.10,000/ shall be remitted to state.
It is made clear that in view of Sec. 421(1) of Cr. P. C even if the accused no.2 and 3 undergo SCCH12 17 C.C.No.12015/2021 the default sentence imposed above, they are not absolved of liability to pay the fine amount.
Bail bond and surety bond of the accused no. 2 and 3 stand cancelled.
Issue free copy of this judgment to accused persons.
